item.title: 'If Trump were president in 2022, there would be no war': Putin after Alaska meeting; US president says no deal with Russia over Ukraine conflict
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin claimed that the Ukraine invasion wouldn't have occurred if Donald Trump were still U.S. President. Putin highlighted his 'good business-like' relationship with Trump, who echoed that the war is 'Biden's war'.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Fraud probe: New Orleans mayor indicted on multiple charges; accused of hiding romantic relationship with her bodyguard
item.description: New Orleans Mayor LaToya Cantrell has been indicted on charges of conspiracy, fraud, and obstruction, concluding a federal investigation into her alleged attempts to conceal a romantic relationship with her bodyguard, Jeffrey Vappie. Prosecutors claim Cantrell and Vappie exploited their positions to hide their relationship and create opportunities to spend time together, including submitting false payroll records.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Saudi Arabia customs seize 28.9 kg of cocaine hidden in frozen meat at Jeddah Islamic Port
item.description: On Friday, ZATCA officials intercepted 28.9 kilograms of cocaine hidden in frozen meat at Jeddah Islamic Port. This follows a June 27 seizure of 732,015 Captagon pills concealed in wardrobes. Utilizing advanced technology and sniffer dogs, ZATCA continues to combat sophisticated smuggling attempts, underscoring Jeddah Port’s critical role in safeguarding Saudi Arabia’s borders and public safety.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 'Trump sees Putin as more powerful': Body language expert on historic handshake; Russian president 'far from cold'
item.description: Body language expert Patty Ann Wood analyzed the historic handshake between Presidents Trump and Putin, noting a blend of warmth, deference, and control. Trump's palm-up gesture suggested he views Putin as more powerful, though he employed his signature close-in handshake, the expert noted. Both leaders maintained eye contact and smiled, indicating warmth.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 'Power move': Trump pulls Putin, pats his back during handshake; social media decodes how tall Putin is
item.description: President Trump's handshake with Putin sparked global interest, analyzed for power dynamics, while height discrepancies fueled speculation about Putin's use of lifts. ​Vladimir Putin is officially 5 feet 7 inches tall, while Trump is 6 feet 3 inches tall. But the visible height difference was not as much as their recorded heights.

item.title: Watch: Black smoke engulfs Manhattan skies after 'explosion' on Upper East Side; over 100 firefighters battle blaze
item.description: A major explosion triggered a 3-alarm fire on Manhattan's Upper East Side near 305 East 95th Street, sending thick black smoke billowing into the sky. Over 100 firefighters responded to the blaze, which started on the roof and spread to multiple penthouses.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Russia–US peace talks: From Bill Clinton to Joe Biden – list of presidents who met Vladimir Putin
item.description: President Putin is set to meet with President Trump in Alaska, marking their first encounter since Trump's second term began. This meeting is crucial amidst the ongoing Russia-Ukraine conflict, especially after Trump's ceasefire deadline passed without resolution. Putin has met with every US president since Bill Clinton, though such meetings have become less frequent due to various geopolitical tensions.

‘Hostile takeover’: DC attorney general files lawsuit against Trump admin; court hearing scheduled for today
item.description: Attorney General Brian Schwalb has filed a lawsuit against the Trump administration, alleging a "hostile takeover" of the Metropolitan Police Department. This action follows Trump's decision to place the MPD under federal control and deploy National Guard troops, citing the need to combat violent crime.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Saudi Arabia travel alert: Travelers carrying prescription drugs must declare and get online permit
item.description: The Saudi Food and Drug Authority (SFDA) has launched a digital process for travelers carrying controlled drugs, including narcotics and psychotropic substances. Through the Controlled Drug System (CDS), travelers can now apply for clearance permits online, upload medical documents, and track their application status. The move aims to support patients while ensuring regulatory compliance and preventing misuse.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 'Honestly': Hillary Clinton says she would nominate Trump for Nobel Peace Prize, only if Ukraine doesn't lose territory
item.description: Hillary Clinton stated she would nominate Donald Trump for the Nobel Peace Prize if he brokers a Russia-Ukraine peace deal that prevents Ukraine from losing territory. This statement precedes Trump's meeting with Vladimir Putin in Alaska, where Trump aims to find a resolution to the conflict. Zelenskyy has urged Trump to convince Russia to end the war.

item.title: One week ultimatum: Pam Bondi orders sanctuary cities to obey immigration laws; threatens legal action
item.description: US Attorney General Pam Bondi, overseeing Washington DC's police, has issued warnings to sanctuary jurisdictions nationwide. These cities, counties, and states face potential legal action if they don't comply with federal immigration laws within a week. Bondi contrasted South Carolina's cooperation with states like New York and California, emphasizing the importance of collaboration for national security and law enforcement.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Another tariff hit: Donald Trump signals levies on chips and steel; semiconductor duties may hit 300%
item.description: President Trump is planning new tariffs on semiconductor chips and steel, potentially shaking global trade. The rates will start low to encourage domestic manufacturing before increasing significantly. Trump hinted at tariffs as high as 100% or even more on semiconductors, with exemptions for companies building in the U.S.
